target_customer: Smartphone owners in Kenya and other emerging markets who run small businesses or are employed but lack credit cards
problem: Few people in Kenya could get short-term credit. Saida scored borrowers from phone activity such as prepaid recharge habits and offered loans repayable in 30 to 60 days. Later the pitch became a bank account with separate pockets of money.
business_model: Consumer lending with interest and fees on short-term loans

founders.name: Kyale Mwendwa
prior_employers: Telecom and mobile banking firms (names not given)
founders.background_notes: Both founders grew up in Kenya and have about seven years of financial services experience in Africa per TechCrunch.

founders.name: Kenneth Ngetha
prior_employers: Telecom and mobile banking firms (names not given)
founders.background_notes: Later moved into venture building at Catalyst Fund per The Condia.

exit.reason: The Condia says the specific reasons remain unclear.

competitors.name: InVenture
competitors.what: Credit scoring and lending using phone data in emerging markets, named as a competitor by TechCrunch

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a credit score from phone usage data and integrating with M-PESA for disbursement and repayment is standard engineering with a hard modeling problem.

defensibility.rationale: Repayment data could compound, but telecoms and M-PESA already held richer phone data and TechCrunch noted they could enter.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch flagged that larger banks or M-PESA could enter. Later digital lenders such as Tala grew in Kenya. No source ties these to Saida's end.

market_need_then: TechCrunch reported about 4,000 loans in the first few months after launch, which shows early demand for small loans in Kenya.

brand_strength.rationale: Little press beyond launch coverage and the parent entity was named Greenshoe, which confused listings.

pivots.from: Short-term loans scored from phone activity
pivots.to: A bank account with dedicated pockets of money
pivots.why: Not stated. YC page now describes the account product; the 2015 launch described lending.

outcome_analysis: Saida launched from YC S15 with a mobile lending app and reported about 4,000 loans within months. By the time YC listed it, the description had moved to a pocketed bank account. The Condia reports the company shut down in January 2022 and says the reasons are unclear, so the cause is not public and no failure factors are assigned.
notes: The directory website field is empty. Seed of 120K is stated by The Condia (opened) and by an Xconomy headline seen only in search results (page returned 503); CB Insights also lists 120K but includes dubious investors and a wrong description. The company is also called Greenshoe in TechCrunch demo day coverage. Shutdown date rests on The Condia alone. Founder education not found. The pivot date is unknown.
